[![Image 42](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/DerryLondonderryStation.jpg/250px-DerryLondonderryStation.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:DerryLondonderryStation.jpg)

[Derry~Londonderry railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_~_Londonderry_railway_station "Derry ~ Londonderry railway station") on the scenic [Belfast-Derry railway line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belfast-Derry_railway_line "Belfast-Derry railway line") run by [Northern Ireland Railways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland_Railways "Northern Ireland Railways")

With 48% of tourists using intracity buses, tubes, trams and metro trains; they are by far the most popular methods of transport.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-:4-41) The next most common methods of transports are taxis and trains (outside town/city) with 27% and 23% respectively.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-:4-41) Trains are used to travel between cities significantly more than aeroplanes, with only 1% of international visitors flying domestically.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-:4-41) This has been attributed to the United Kingdom's vast rail network being the most economical way to travel.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-42) Despite [Uber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uber "Uber") being in a legal battle to operate in London, the rise of Uber and other [ride-sharing companies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ridesharing_company "Ridesharing company") throughout the United Kingdom has led to them being used by 9% of international tourists and they are expected to further increase, reducing the market share of other methods of transport.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-43)

## Events, festivals and exhibitions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Events, festivals and exhibitions")]

The United Kingdom plays host to a variety of events that attract both international and domestic tourists.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-44) Some of the United Kingdom's most famous festivals include [Notting Hill Carnival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notting_Hill_Carnival "Notting Hill Carnival"), [Glastonbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glastonbury "Glastonbury") and the [Edinburgh Fringe Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh_Festival_Fringe "Edinburgh Festival Fringe").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-45) These festivals not only hold cultural significance but are also a major economic component of the United Kingdom's tourist industry, with [Glastonbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glastonbury "Glastonbury") alone contributing £100 million to the economy annually.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-46) The beauty, real estate and arms industries are some of the many industries that hold trade shows and exhibitions year-round throughout the United Kingdom, with the majority being held in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") or [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham "Birmingham"). [VisitBritain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VisitBritain "VisitBritain") has estimated in 2015 there were 65 million day visits centred around events, festivals and exhibitions and in total, they accounted for 5% of all tourist day visits and a net spend of £3.6 billion.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-47)

## Marketing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Marketing")]

[![Image 43](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b5/Minister_for_Sport_Hugh_Robertson_at_launch_of_GREAT_campaign%2C_Australia_%286841281192%29.jpg/250px-Minister_for_Sport_Hugh_Robertson_at_launch_of_GREAT_campaign%2C_Australia_%286841281192%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Minister_for_Sport_Hugh_Robertson_at_launch_of_GREAT_campaign,_Australia_(6841281192).jpg)

Launch of GREAT campaign, Australia

In 2011, [VisitBritain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VisitBritain "VisitBritain") launched GREAT, one of a £100 million marketing campaign, promoting the United Kingdom through culture, heritage, sport, music, countryside, food and shopping.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-48) The campaign has successfully reached over 145 countries and united both the public and private sectors to generate growth and jobs.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-49) Overall, inbound and domestic marketing have generated £1 billion in additional visitor spend, of which, £800 million can be attributed to the GREAT campaign.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-50)

## Shopping

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Shopping")]

[![Image 44](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Harrods_at_night.jpg/250px-Harrods_at_night.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Harrods_at_night.jpg)

Harrods at night

Shopping is one of the most common activities for overseas visitors to the United Kingdom with 58% of all visits and 70% of leisure visits involving shopping.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-51) Each year, roughly 277,000 people travel to the United Kingdom for the primary reason of personal shopping.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-:5-52) The total spend of these visits is around £168 million.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-:5-52) The most commonly purchased items are clothes and shoes with just over 40% of visitors purchasing at least one item of clothing or a pair of shoes.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-:5-52)

Ornamental souvenirs representing items found in the United Kingdom such as post office boxes, [black cabs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hackney_carriage#Black_cabs "Hackney carriage") and London buses are commonly found in souvenir shops over the United Kingdom.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-53) Other examples of commonly purchased souvenirs include: [Union Jack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Jack "Union Jack") branded goods, items from famous department stores like [Harrods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrods "Harrods") and [Selfridges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selfridges "Selfridges") and memorabilia surrounding the [British royal family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_royal_family "British royal family").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_the_United_Kingdom#cite_note-54)

Maybe there may be two tied or just top two. Then among those two pick the one with largest median population in 2019.

Thus we need region arrival data for 2018-2019.

Similarly need population data for each region in 2019; compute median population per region (median of all countries' total population (both sexes) in 2019). Then among the two regions with largest decrease, choose one with larger median pop.
